en.headline: Government raises 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.5–4.5% after strong first half
en.dek: The revision follows a 5.1 per cent expansion in the first six months, the strongest half-year performance in nearly five years, driven by robust AI-related exports.
body: The government on Friday raised its full-year real GDP growth forecast for 2026 to a range of 3.5 to 4.5 per cent, up from the previous projection of 2.5 to 3.5 per cent issued in May.

Government Economist Irina Fan said the upward revision reflected the stronger-than-expected outturn in the first half and the near-term outlook. Real GDP grew 4.3 per cent year on year in the second quarter after a 5.9 per cent rise in the first three months, lifting the first-half expansion to 5.1 per cent — the best half-yearly figure in almost five years.

Exports of goods surged 28.9 per cent in real terms in the second quarter, supported by global demand for artificial-intelligence-related electronic products. Private consumption expenditure rose 2.8 per cent and overall investment increased 4.4 per cent. Fan said the economy should see solid growth in the second half, though external risks including geopolitical tensions and trade protectionism require close monitoring.

zh.headline: 政府上調2026年經濟增長預測至3.5%至4.5%
zh.dek: 上半年實質本地生產總值增長5.1%，為近五年來最強勁半年度表現，主要受人工智能相關產品出口帶動。
body: 政府周五將2026年全年實質本地生產總值增長預測，由五月覆檢時的2.5%至3.5%向上修訂至3.5%至4.5%。
政府經濟顧問范婉兒表示，修訂反映上半年較預期強勁的實際數字及短期展望。實質本地生產總值第二季按年增長4.3%，第一季增長5.9%，上半年整體增長5.1%，是近五年來最強勁的半年度表現。
全球對人工智能相關電子產品需求殷切，帶動整體貨物出口第二季按年實質急升28.9%。私人消費開支上升2.8%，整體投資開支增4.4%。范婉兒指下半年經濟應可見穩健增長，但外圍地緣政治緊張及貿易保護主義等風險須密切監察。
